name: Tukudede
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Checked: Hull 2002, The Languages of East Timor: Some Basic Facts (read via archive.org) - Tokodede section has no stress statement; no grammar of Tukudede located.

sources.citation: Williams-van Klinken, Catharina. 2020. Selected bibliography of works on languages of Timor-Leste. Dili Institute of Technology.
sources.note: Bibliographic aid: the Tokodede section lists only Lekede'e Study Group 2006 -- confirms no grammar/phonology of Tokodede exists in English or Portuguese as of 2020.

sources.citation: Instituto Nacional de Linguistica (UNTL) website, 2007 Internet Archive copy (, projects, research bulletin).
sources.note: East Timor Language Profiles published = Dili Tetum, Waimaha, Galoli, Baikenu, Southern Mambai, Makasai, Fataluku: no Tokodede profile. SLCET contents show Hull 1998 and Hull 2001 (print only). No Tokodede project listed.

sources.citation: Klamer, Marian. 2002. Timor-Leste survey word lists: Tokodede (Mauboke, west of Liquica, 2002-05-10; speaker M. Ataidi do Rego, 70). Unpublished; published as lect tuku1254 in Kaiping, Edwards & Klamer (eds.) 2019, LexiRumah 3.0.0 (CLDF).
sources.note: Wordlist only, no prose. 276 IPA forms, 105 carry a primary-stress mark. My tabulation: stress mark on the penultimate vowel in 81/99 polysyllables (kaˈtana, giˈniu, kuˈluta, tuˈnuru, kəˈdɛʔɛ, lɑpɑˈrɛta..); all 18 apparent 'final' cases end in a vowel sequence (sɑˈbɑi, kɑˈlɑu, boˈloi, pɑˈrɑe), a long vowel from *-Vn loss (kɔˈmɔː, meˈgɛː, biˈriː, kaˈbeː) or a closed syllable (kuˈmaːt, luˈrɔn, kuˈmus, kmeˈʔɑt) -- consistent with stress on the penultimate vocalic mora. Inference from data, not a statement.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid tuku1254 reference list (langdoc query).
sources.note: Only 3 references in total (Capell 1944 x2, Hull 1998); no grammar, sketch or phonology entry.

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Owen Edwards. 2026. The Austronesian languages of eastern Indonesia and Timor-Leste. Berlin: Language Science Press (langsci 526). ch.5 'Central Timor', pp.253-271; Appendix data-source table.
sources.note: Historical phonology only for Tokodede (Liquica variety; *n > zero with compensatory vowel lengthening, Table 5.20; *b > h Liquica/Bazartete vs v Maubara). No Tokodede stress statement. Appendix lists the only Tokodede data sources as 'Klamer 2002, Lekede'e Study Group 2006'. Areal remark p.115: 'penultimate stress is the normal rule for Wallacean languages' (not language-specific).

sources.citation: Esperanca, Joao Paulo T. 2006. 'Peneer meselo laa Literatura kidia-laa Timor' (first published Tokodede text, Varzea de Letras, Dec 2005; blog repost with Portuguese/Tokodede preface) and related posts; Esperanca 2025, Conselho telu / Tres conselhos (tokodede los portugues), 34 pp., ISBN 9789403790114.
sources.note: Texts only. Preface: orthography 'ainda provisoria'; announces 'um pequeno manual sobre este idioma, a publicar no futuro proximo' (not known to have appeared). Orthography uses INL-style acute on non-penultimate stress in loans (Likisá, orijinál, manuál) and double vowels for length -- no explicit stress statement.

sources.citation: Lekede'e Study Group. 2006. Disionariu Lia (Dalen) Tokodede - Tetun - Ingles. Liquica: Lekedee Study Group / Timor Lorosa'e Nippon Culture Center.
sources.note: Tetun-language introduction (sections 1-10: Likisa/Bazartete/Maubara varieties, h ~ v correspondence, letters used, loans, pronouns, numerals, gender terms) and c. 4,600 entries; no mention of stress/accent (a full-text search for stress/accent asentu/toniku/silaba = 0); orthography without accent marks except sporadic acute on Tetun glosses.

sources.citation: Hull, Geoffrey. 2002 [rev. to 2006]. The Languages of East Timor: Some Basic Facts. Instituto Nacional de Linguistica, UNTL (web/PDF), sec. 11 'Tokodede'.
sources.note: Location, lexical strata, 'simple isolating morphology similar to that of Mambai', numerals 1-10 (hohoru with acute on final syllable per INL convention); no stress statement.

sources.citation: Capell, Arthur. 1944. Peoples and languages of Timor [Part I]. Oceania 14(3): 191-219; [Part III] Oceania 15(1): 19-48.
sources.note: Part I ethnography; Part III sound laws and comparative morphology (pronouns, numerals, verb) of the 'Indonesian' languages incl. Tukudede; nothing on stress/accent (the 'Stress.' heading in the 15(1) scanned belongs to the Berndts' Ooldea article in the same issue).

sources.citation: Capell, Arthur. 1944. Peoples and languages of Timor [Part II]. Oceania 14(4): 311-337.
sources.note: No rule. p.313 has a three-line 'Tukudede' entry (location, c. 45,000 speakers, 'fairly closely related to Tetum'). p.329 states only the transcription convention: 'In the vocabularies a more exact transcription of the vowels has been given.. and the stress has been marked by an acute accent before the stressed syllable.' The comparative vocabulary pp.330-337 has a Tukudede column with stress marks (p.330: 'hinɛ, a'nama, 'kaka'manɛ, mɔ'ta:, ga'lama, 'tiligroa, 'nipa, 'ibɔn 'kluta, 'lim 'tanɛ, 'hiru 'mata, 'ka:bu, 'lɛlɔ, 'hula, 'hitu, 'gɛlu, 'uran) -- primary data, overwhelmingly penultimate,…

sources.citation: Mandala, Halus. 2012. Relasi genetis bahasa-bahasa Timor [Genetic relationship of the languages of Timor]. Mabasan 6(2): 1-17. Mataram: Kantor Bahasa Provinsi Nusa Tenggara Barat. doi:10.26499/mab.v6i2.225 (DOI registered 2019 for the 2012 issue). In Indonesian.

tone.summary: Lexicostatistic subgrouping of 7 Timor languages with segmental sound changes and Proto-Timor phoneme reconstruction; no passage on tone, pitch, stress or prosody for Tokodede or any language.

sources.citation: Hull, Geoffrey. 2001. A morphological overview of the Timoric Sprachbund. Studies in Languages and Cultures of East Timor 4: 98-205. (Instituto Nacional de Linguistica / UWS Macarthur)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only pan-Timoric structural survey by the one linguist who worked on Tokodede systematically; if any published sentence on Tokodede (or general Timoric/Ramelaic) stress exists, it is most likely in its phonological preliminaries or transcription notes.
sources.venue: Studies in Languages and Cultures of East Timor

sources.citation: Edwards, Owen. 2019. Reintroducing Welaun. Oceanic Linguistics 58(1): 31-58.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Modern first-hand description of the closest documented relative (Welaun) with systematic comparison to Kemak and Tokodede; may contain a comparative remark on Central Timor stress and cites any unpublished Tokodede field data.

sources.citation: Esperanca, Joao Paulo T. [announced 2006]. 'Pequeno manual' da lingua tocodede (Liquica dialect). Apparently unpublished.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Announced in the preface to the first published Tokodede text by a trained linguist fluent in the language; would be the only pedagogical description and would state the orthographic stress convention. Existence unverified.
